key_insight: Compact VLMs (e.g., 2B and 8B) can reach strong vision-language performance without relying on heavy contrastive (CLIP-style) pretraining by using LLM-aligned vision encoder training that removes an objective mismatch between vision and language modules.
problem_solved: Addresses the challenge of deploying state-of-the-art VLMs on compute-constrained devices by questioning the need for large contrastively pretrained vision encoders and exploring efficient alternatives for compact models.
method: Design and evaluate compact VLMs (2B and 8B) to probe efficiency and performance limits under constrained compute budgets.

Replace or reframe CLIP/SigLIP-style contrastive pretraining with LLM-aligned supervision — training vision encoders with objectives compatible with generative LLMs (an LLM-based vision-encoder approach) to fix the objective mismatch.
Systematically compare performance vs. compute/size trade-offs across benchmarks to quantify gains in efficiency and deployment feasibility.
impact: Shows a practical pathway to build high-quality, deployable VLMs for mobile and edge applications by removing dependence on massive contrastive pretraining and aligning vision encoders with LLM objectives — lowering compute, latency, and engineering cost for practitioners.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: side-by-side comparison of CLIP-style contrastive pipeline vs. Penguin-VL's LLM-aligned vision-encoder pipeline.
Efficiency vs. performance plot: model size (2B, 8B, larger baselines) on x-axis, accuracy/benchmark score on y-axis, with compute/latency overlays.
Objective mismatch flowchart: illustrate how contrastive loss diverges from LLM generative objectives and how LLM-based supervision reconciles them.
Deployment infographic: icons showing reduced compute, lower memory footprint, and edge/mobile device compatibility
paper_title: Penguin-VL: Exploring the Efficiency Limits of VLM with LLM-based Vision Encoders
paper_authors: Boqiang Zhang, Lei Ke, Ruihan Yang, Qi Gao, Tianyuan Qu
